back: m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁) = rise/run. Undefined when x₁ = x₂ (vertical line).
m = tan θ, where θ is the angle measured anti-clockwise from positive x-axis. θ ∈ [0°, 180°).
Two non-vertical lines are parallel iff their slopes are equal: m₁ = m₂.
Two lines are perpendicular iff m₁ · m₂ = −1 (negative reciprocal).
tan θ = |(m₂ − m₁)/(1 + m₁m₂)|. Gives the acute angle. Denominator = 0 ⟹ θ = 90°.
y − y₁ = m(x − x₁). Use when you have a point and slope.
y − y₁ = [(y₂−y₁)/(x₂−x₁)](x − x₁). Use when you have two points.
y = mx + c. Slope = m, y-intercept = c. Line crosses y-axis at (0, c).
x/a + y/b = 1. x-intercept = a, y-intercept = b. Both must be non-zero.
Ax + By + C = 0. Every line can be written this way. Slope = −A/B (if B ≠ 0).
d = |Ax₁ + By₁ + C|/√(A² + B²). Line must be in general form Ax+By+C=0. Absolute value ensures d ≥ 0.
For Ax+By+C₁=0 and Ax+By+C₂=0: d = |C₁−C₂|/√(A²+B²). Coefficients A, B must match.
From Ax + By + C = 0: slope m = −A/B. Quick: flip the x and y coefficients, negate.

front: Slope of horizontal vs vertical line
back: Horizontal (y = c): slope = 0. Vertical (x = c): slope undefined (not ∞).
